Messages.Author: Joshua Duffin
Messages.Body:
"Wouter Kuyper" <Wouter...@yahoo.com> wrote in message
news:44a2da05.04040...@posting.google.com...

[re Coagulated Entity vs Bum's Rush comparison]

> I think there is quite a difference in the cards. One says:"THIS"
> action, and THIS combat.
> The other says: this vampire gets +x strength and +x capacity. It
> never says for how long.

> compare it to:
> Death of my concience:
> Requires a vampire with a capacity above 5. Do not replace this card
> until after combat. Play before strikes are chosen. [pot] Burn up to 4
> cards in your hand. For each card you burn this way, this vampire gets
> +1 strength for the remainder of combat. Do not replace these cards
> until after combat. [POT] As above, but this vampire gets +2 strength
> for the remainder of combat for each card you burn this way.
>
> This says for the remainder of combat.
>
> All cards say for how long it counts...or say it should be put on the
> vampire. This one doesn't fit in either....
>
> Or am i missing something?

Probably, yes. :-)

By default, action modifiers and reactions last for the duration of the
action (per rulebook). Most of them don't have timing specified on
their card texts, for that reason.

By a ruling (23-Jun-1998), combat cards default to lasting for the
duration of the current round. Combat cards that have other durations
than that must now specify in card text (so, a lot of them do).

Action cards default to being done with when their action is resolved,
unless they have card text saying "put this card in play" (or "put this
card on the acting vampire" or some such). I don't think there's a
general ruling on this one, but there is a specific clarification (?) on
Coagulated Entity: [LSJ 18-Dec-2001]

www.google.com/groups?selm=3C1FF593.9D751F43%40white-wolf.com

Also, compare to Border Skirmish: "Each other Methuselah discards one
card at random from his or her hand, and this anarch untaps at the end
of the turn."

You wouldn't assume that this anarch untaps at the end of *every* turn
as a result of playing this card, would you? Same reason: normally an
action's effects end when the action is done, unless the card says
otherwise.

Josh
